source: MAFF General Directorate of Agriculture, banana cultivation techniques manual, 2019, section III.2 (land/hole preparation for planting)
text: Preferred land for banana is soil previously used for legumes, cleared of existing vegetation and left to rest for about 10 days before digging planting holes. Holes are dug in a staggered (checkerboard) pattern rather than a strict grid, each hole roughly 50 x 50cm square and about 50cm deep. Recommended spacing is 3-6m between rows and 2-6m between plants within a row, with the exact spacing chosen according to variety vigor and soil fertility — vigorous varieties or richer soil can tolerate wider spacing, while smaller varieties on poorer soil can be planted closer. Topsoil removed while digging should be kept separate and mixed with organic matter/compost before being used to backfill around the sucker at planting time.
